title: What Actually Matters
gist_ar: مقال عن تقييم المدارس: الكاتب بيقول إن اللي بيتقاس مش هو اللي مهم.
text:
It is not the size of a school's budget that predicts what its pupils learn.
That much is well established. What is less often said, and what this article
sets out to underline, is that we know which factor does predict it and have
chosen to measure something else.

The crux is teacher retention. Schools that keep their staff for five years
outperform comparable schools that do not, and the gap is decisive rather than
subtle. It is precisely this that our inspection framework fails to capture. What
the framework prioritises is documentation: lesson plans, marking policies,
evidence of intervention. All of these are visible in a single day's visit, which
is, one suspects, the actual criterion.

Above all, it is worth noting what the published rankings reward. A school can
rise two bands by improving its paperwork while losing a third of its teachers,
and several have. Little wonder that headteachers pinpoint compliance rather than
retention as their priority. They are not confused about what matters. They are
responding accurately to what is counted.

There is a striking asymmetry here. The significance of retention is
acknowledged in every policy document; the aspect of school life it depends on —
whether teaching there is bearable — appears in none of them. Namely: workload,
autonomy, and whether a complaint from a parent is investigated or simply
forwarded.

The essence of the problem is therefore not measurement error. It is that we
have a metric which is cheap, defensible and nearly irrelevant, and another which
is expensive, contestable and nearly sufficient. We have made the choice any
institution makes, and we describe it as rigour.

questions.q: What does the writer identify as the crux?
Why does the writer say headteachers prioritise compliance?
questions.q_ar: ليه الكاتب بيقول إن المديرين بيهتموا بالالتزام الشكلي؟
options: They are responding accurately to what is actually counted
They do not understand what matters
They are required to by law

questions.q: What is the writer's tone when saying inspections favour what is visible in one day?
questions.q_ar: إيه نبرة الكاتب لما قال إن التفتيش بيفضّل اللي بيبان في يوم واحد؟
options: Approving; a single visit is efficient
Dryly sceptical — 'one suspects' signals the real motive
Uncertain; the writer does not know why

questions.q: How does the writer characterise the final choice between the two metrics?
questions.q_ar: الكاتب وصف الاختيار بين المقياسين إزاي؟
options: A measurement error that can be corrected
An institutional preference for the cheap metric, presented as rigour
